nodes.referent: Jan Ignacy Niecislaw Baudouin de Courtenay (1845-1929), Polish linguist of French-Huguenot noble descent who held professorships at Kazan, Dorpat/Tartu, Krakow, and St Petersburg/Petrograd, and co-founded (with his student Mikolaj Kruszewski) the Kazan School of linguistics. Credited with an early, psychologically grounded theory of the phoneme, and with distinguishing purely phonetic sound alternations from morphologically/grammatically conditioned ones in work of the 1890s -- commonly cited in histories of linguistics as anticipating the structural/synchronic concerns later systematized by 20th-century phonology. Also worked on Slavic dialectology and general linguistic theory. Not to be confused with any other bearer of the same uncommon compound surname, and distinct from his student and collaborator Mikolaj Kruszewski and from the later Prague School phonologists (Trubetzkoy, Jakobson) whose work he anticipated but did not belong to.
